deck: JavaScript & TypeScript: Zero to Mastery · 21 · Discriminated Unions & Exhaustiveness

notes.title: area(shape)
notes.quote: The never type is assignable to every type; however, no type is assignable to never (except never itself). This means you can use narrowing and rely on never turning up to do exhaustive checking in a switch statement.
notes.type_tests:
// @ts-expect-error: a triangle is not a Shape
area({ kind: "triangle", base: 1, height: 2 });

notes.back:
No. `const unreachable: never = shape` fails: the triangle type is not assignable to type 'never' — there is no case for "triangle".

Why: After the circle and square cases, the only thing shape can still be is a triangle, so it isn't never. Add the missing case and it compiles.

Docs: TypeScript Handbook — Narrowing — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/narrowing.html
notes.quote: For example, adding a default to our getArea function which tries to assign the shape to never will not raise an error when every possible case has been handled.

notes.title: Type the counter's actions
notes.quote: Discriminated unions are useful for more than just talking about circles and squares.
